To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the benefits and risks of the protection and commercialization process of academic research are diverse and conflicting; 2) the benefits and the risks are related to the specific context of the university and the research area, and are not generalizable; 3) the benefits and risk are not mutually exclusive; and 4) the benefits and/or the risks can be more or less important depending on the university and the area of knowledge.

(a) the benefits of patenting and licensing are not as clear and evident as the risks; (b) patenting and licensing of academic research results is not an easy task; (c) patenting and licencing is not a panacea for the problems of universities; (d) patenting and commercialization of university research results may have negative impacts on research and teaching activities.
the benefits and risks of IPRs are not mutually exclusive, but complementary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the role of IPRs in the research process?
the following questions: what are the benefits of IPRS for academic research, for the university and for society?
a discussion that has been going on in the last two decades, and which is still not fully resolved, about the benefits and risks of IPRs for universities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the benefits of patenting and licensing are still not clear, and that the risks are considerable, particularly when they affect teaching and research activities.
the benefits of the protection and commercialization process of university research results are still unclear and that the risks are real and significant.
the benefits of commercialization of research are still not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the benefits of patenting and licensing of academic research results are not yet clear, but that the risks are evident.
IPRs are an instrument that can be useful for universities to generate resources, but it is not the only one.

, in order to understand the benefits and risks of the protection and commercialization processes of academic research, it is necessary to consider the context in which these activities are carried out.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IPRs are a double-edged sword, with benefits and risks for universities.
the benefits of the protection and commercialization process are not necessarily positive for the research university, and the risk of negative impacts is real.
the protection and commercialization process is not neutral and that the impact of this process on the traditional activities of universities must be carefully assessed.
